journal_name: IEEE Transactions on Dependable and Secure Computing

abstracts.abstract: This paper presents a unified formal framework that fundamentally reconciles fault tolerance and security analysis in cyber-physical systems, addressing a long-standing dichotomy in dependable computing research. Unlike traditional approaches that treat reliability and security as orthogonal concerns, we propose a probabilistic game-theoretic model that captures the adversarial interactions between fault tolerance mechanisms and security attacks within a single mathematical formalism. Our framework introduces novel concepts of security-aware reliability and reliability-aware security, enabling the systematic analysis of trade-offs that were previously intractable. We define formal verification conditions for systems to achieve joint security and dependability guarantees, and prove fundamental impossibility results that characterize the inherent limitations of any defense mechanism. The theoretical contributions include new theorems establishing necessary and sufficient conditions for the coexistence of fault tolerance and intrusion detection in Byzantine environments. We demonstrate the framework's applicability through case studies in power grid control systems and autonomous vehicle networks, where our analysis reveals previously unknown vulnerabilities arising from the interaction of reliability mechanisms with security protocols. This work establishes a new paradigm for designing and verifying dependable systems that must simultaneously resist both random faults and malicious attacks.

This paper presents significant theoretical improvements to formal verification techniques for cryptographic protocol implementations, addressing the verification gap between protocol specifications and their implementations in modern secure computing systems. While existing symbolic verification methods achieve strong theoretical guarantees, they suffer from high computational complexity that limits their scalability to real-world protocols. We introduce a novel compositional verification approach based on a refined abstraction-refinement framework that reduces verification complexity from exponential to polynomial time for a large class of security protocols. Our method leverages new algebraic properties of cryptographic primitives discovered through systematic analysis of protocol structures, enabling modular verification that preserves soundness while dramatically improving efficiency. We prove new theoretical bounds showing that our approach achieves O(n²) complexity compared to the O(2ⁿ) complexity of prior methods, where n represents the number of protocol participants. The improved framework extends naturally to handle network security protocols with concurrent sessions and provides stronger soundness guarantees for privacy preservation. Experimental results on standardized cryptographic protocols demonstrate that our approach verifies protocols that were previously intractable, including complex key exchange mechanisms with forward secrecy requirements. This work significantly advances the practical applicability of formal methods for security verification in systems requiring cryptographic protection.

This paper introduces ResilienceChain, a novel system architecture that fundamentally reimagines intrusion detection through blockchain-based distributed consensus, representing a paradigm shift in network security for enterprise systems. Traditional centralized intrusion detection systems suffer from single points of failure and are vulnerable to targeted attacks that compromise their detection capabilities. ResilienceChain distributes the intrusion detection function across a consortium of nodes using a Byzantine-fault-tolerant consensus mechanism that ensures detection integrity even when a significant fraction of nodes are compromised. The system employs a novel reputation-based anomaly detection algorithm that achieves sub-second detection latency while maintaining high accuracy, addressing a fundamental trade-off between detection speed and precision that has limited prior approaches. Our architecture introduces hierarchical detection layers that combine lightweight edge analysis with deep semantic inspection at consensus nodes, enabling energy-efficient deployment across heterogeneous networks including IoT environments. We provide a complete implementation with optimized consensus protocols that achieve over 10,000 transactions per second throughput while maintaining detection accuracy above 99.5% across diverse attack scenarios. Security analysis proves that ResilienceChain maintains liveness and safety properties under various adversarial conditions including coordinated attacks and network partitions. This work establishes a new design paradigm for cyber-physical system security where trust emerges from distributed consensus rather than centralized authority.

This paper presents SecureVault, a significantly improved hardware security architecture for protecting sensitive computations in cloud computing environments, addressing critical vulnerabilities in existing secure enclave designs. While trusted execution environments have emerged as a cornerstone for secure computing, prior implementations suffer from measurable side-channel leakage and lack adequate protection against speculative execution attacks that compromise software security. SecureVault introduces a multi-layered protection architecture that combines hardware-enforced isolation with novel microarchitectural modifications that eliminate speculative timing channels while maintaining performance within 5% of unprotected execution. The system design incorporates a certified information flow tracking mechanism that operates at hardware speed, enabling runtime detection of potential data leakage without the overhead of software-based monitoring. We implement SecureVault on a RISC-V processor with custom security extensions, achieving full-system protection for complex workloads including cryptographic operations and secure multi-party computation. Performance evaluation demonstrates 3.2x throughput improvement over Intel SGX for equivalent security guarantees, while providing stronger confidentiality guarantees for hardware security against physical attacks. The architecture includes a formal verification backend that proves security properties of the hardware design, bridging the gap between formal methods and practical hardware security. SecureVault significantly advances the state-of-the-art in hardware security for cloud environments, providing practical protection against both software and hardware attacks.
